chapter: Ch. 2 — What Actually Happens During Inference
evidence: Instance 1 (PDF p.58, book p.34): "actual sustained bandwidth for weight-read kernels may be 60–80% of peak [2°: industry rule of thumb][HYPOTHESIS][UNMEASURED] — not measured or cited here." Instance 2 (PDF p.56, book p.32): "the [2°] industry range is 30–40%, and the 35% point is the book's chosen planning value." The book's own Axis-1 definition: "[2°] — reputable second-hand: textbook, survey, or independent benchmark" (PDF p.20, Preface) and "[2°] reputable second-hand (textbook, survey, independent benchmark)" (Table 4-2 Note 1, PDF p.104). Corroborating internal tension: Ch 2 §2.7 (PDF p.60, book p.36) lists the same quantity (sustained HBM bandwidth for weight-read kernels) as "a hypothesis to be measured on real hardware before it is cited" — i.e., the book itself says the figure is not yet citable, yet §2.5 assigns it second-hand provenance.
issue: Provenance-label mismatch by the book's own taxonomy (recurrence: 2 instances in Ch. 2). [2°] is defined as a nameable reputable second-hand source (textbook/survey/independent benchmark), but both usages attach [2°] to uncited industry folklore — and the first sentence explicitly concedes "not measured or cited here", which contradicts the provenance claim the tag makes. The epistemic-axis tags ([HYPOTHESIS], [UNMEASURED]) are correct; the Axis-1 [2°] tag is the defect. No numeric harm results (the values are flagged unmeasured and used only as sensitivity context), so P3.
fix_instruction: For each instance, either cite the specific second-hand source (named survey or independent benchmark) so [2°] resolves per its definition, or relabel as [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS] (keeping [UNMEASURED] on Axis 3) or [UNRESOLVED], since no citable second-hand source currently exists; align §2.5 with §2.7's treatment of the same quantity.
